subject: Agriculture
title: Photoperiod Insensitivity
description: A quick win: understand Photoperiod Insensitivity.

hook.text: Most crops flower based on day length. That makes them useless if you move them to a new latitude.

buildup.text: A rice variety bred in the Philippines only blooms when days are 12 hours. Plant it in India—different timing.

discovery.text: Breeders selected for photoperiod insensitivity—varieties that flower based on age, not sunlight hours.

twist.text: This single trait let Green Revolution varieties spread across latitudes. One seed worked from Pakistan to Brazil.

climax.text: Without photoperiod insensitivity, high-yield varieties would have stayed local. This trait made them global.

punchline.text: Ignoring the sun made these crops universally useful.

quiz.question: What is photoperiod insensitivity in crops?
options: Flowering based on age rather than day length, allowing growth at any latitude
